{{Recipe summary
| Category = Duck recipes
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Duck|Duck]]

== Ingredients ==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]]. (about 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]]) [[cookbook:duck|duck]] leg portions with thighs attached, excess fat trimmed and reserved
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] plus ⅛ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
* ½ teaspoon freshly-ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|black pepper]]
* 10 [[cookbook:garlic|garlic]] cloves
* 4 [[Cookbook:Bay Leaf|bay leaves]]
* 4 sprigs fresh [[cookbook:thyme|thyme]]
* 1½ teaspoon black [[Cookbook:Pepper|peppercorns]]
* ½ teaspoon table [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]

== Procedure ==
# Lay the duck leg portions on a platter, skin side down. Sprinkle with 1 tablespoon of the salt and the black pepper.
# Place the garlic cloves, bay leaves, and sprigs of thyme on each of 2 leg portions. Lay the remaining 2 leg portions, flesh to flesh, on top.
# Put the fat from the ducks in the bottom of a glass or plastic container. Top with the sandwiched leg portions, and sprinkle with the remaining ⅛ teaspoon salt.
# Cover and refrigerate for 12 hours.
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 200°F (95°C).
# Remove the duck from the refrigerator. Remove the garlic, bay leaves, thyme, and duck fat and set aside.
# Rinse the duck with cool water, rubbing off some of the salt and pepper. Pat dry with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]]. 
# Put the garlic, bay leaves, thyme, and duck fat in the bottom of an [[Cookbook:Enamel|enameled]] [[Cookbook:Cast Iron|cast-iron]] pot. Sprinkle evenly with the peppercorns and table salt. 
# Lay the duck on top, skin side down. Add the olive oil.
# Cover and [[cookbook:bake|bake]] for 12 to 14 hours, or until the meat pulls away from the bone.
# Remove the duck from the fat. [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the fat and set aside. 
# To store the duck confit, place the duck leg portions in a container, cover with the cooking fat, and store in the refrigerator. Alternately, pick the meat from the bones and place it in a stoneware container. Cover the meat with a thin layer of some of the strained fat.
# Store in the refrigerator for up to 1 month. The excess oil can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator and used like [[cookbook:butter|butter]] for cooking. The tinge of duck taste in the oil is wonderful.
